canh-muop-nam-bo-ngot-chay.name: Luffa, Straw Mushroom, and Malabar Spinach Soup
aliases: Vegetarian Luffa and Straw Mushroom Soup
canh-muop-nam-bo-ngot-chay.serving_basis: A pot of soup to serve four with rice.
canh-muop-nam-bo-ngot-chay.description: Luffa, straw mushrooms, and Malabar spinach make a gentle vegetarian soup with natural sweetness. Briefly sautéing the luffa first brings out its aroma while the greens stay bright.
canh-muop-nam-bo-ngot-chay.finished_dish: The luffa is tender but intact, the mushrooms are plump, and the greens are just cooked. The clear broth tastes naturally sweet and lightly seasoned.
canh-muop-nam-bo-ngot-chay.serving: Ladle into bowls while hot and finish with pepper if desired. Serve with rice and tofu or another vegetable dish.
tips: Choose firm luffa with evenly green skin.
Cook the greens only until wilted and bright; avoid letting them turn mushy.
Season gradually because vegetarian seasoning brands vary in saltiness.
search_terms: vegetarian luffa mushroom Malabar spinach soup

canh-muop-nam-bo-ngot-chay.media_alt_text: A clear vegetarian soup with luffa, straw mushrooms, and Malabar spinach.
canh-muop-nam-bo-ngot-chay.time_note: About 25 minutes; the water quantity is adjusted for four bowls of soup.

Use enough for a four-serving pot of soup.

preparation_steps: Peel the luffa, rinse it, and cut it into bite-size rounds. Trim the straw mushrooms, rinse briefly, and halve the larger ones.
Pick the Malabar spinach leaves, rinse away any grit, and drain well.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pot. Add the luffa and gently stir over medium heat for about 3 minutes, until it turns slightly translucent and fragrant.
Add the straw mushrooms, vegetarian seasoning, and water. Bring to a gentle boil, skimming any foam.
Stir in the Malabar spinach just until wilted and bright green. Taste, finish with pepper if desired, then turn off the heat.

goi-rau-ma-chay-nam-bao-ngu.name: Vegetarian Pennywort Salad with Oyster Mushrooms
aliases: Pennywort Salad with Vegetarian Oyster Mushrooms
goi-rau-ma-chay-nam-bao-ngu.serving_basis: One shared salad for three people.
goi-rau-ma-chay-nam-bao-ngu.description: Crisp pennywort is tossed with savory stir-fried oyster mushrooms and a light sweet-and-sour dressing. This salad works as the vegetable dish or a starter in a vegetarian meal.
goi-rau-ma-chay-nam-bao-ngu.finished_dish: The pennywort stays crisp, the lime dressing is gently balanced, and the oyster mushrooms are tender, savory, and well seasoned.
goi-rau-ma-chay-nam-bao-ngu.serving: Dress just before serving so the greens stay crisp. Serve alongside rice or as a vegetarian starter.
tips: Rinse the pennywort several times and drain it thoroughly before dressing.
Cook the mushrooms separately and let them cool slightly before adding them.
Taste the dressing first, then adjust lime or sugar to preference.
search_terms: vegetarian pennywort salad with oyster mushrooms

goi-rau-ma-chay-nam-bao-ngu.media_alt_text: A pennywort salad topped with stir-fried oyster mushrooms and sliced chili.
goi-rau-ma-chay-nam-bao-ngu.time_note: About 30 minutes including washing the greens and preparing the dressing.
ingredients: Remove damaged leaves, rinse thoroughly, and drain well.
Trim the base, tear into bite-size pieces, and drain before cooking.
Deseed and slice; reduce or omit for a mild salad.
Divide between the mushrooms and dressing.
preparation_steps: Pick through the pennywort, rinse away soil, and drain thoroughly. Tear the oyster mushrooms into bite-size pieces and slice the chili.
Stir together the lime juice, sugar, and part of the vegetarian seasoning until dissolved. Taste for a gentle sweet-and-sour balance.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and stir-fry the mushrooms until tender and lightly golden. Season with soy sauce and the remaining vegetarian seasoning, then let them cool slightly.
Toss the pennywort with the dressing just before serving. Arrange the mushrooms on top, add chili to taste, and serve.

rau-cu-xao-thap-cam-chay.name: Vegetarian Mixed Vegetable Stir-Fry
rau-cu-xao-thap-cam-chay.serving_basis: One shared vegetable dish for two people.
rau-cu-xao-thap-cam-chay.description: Broccoli, cauliflower, baby corn, peas, and shiitake are briefly blanched, then quickly tossed in a savory soy and vegetarian oyster sauce. This keeps the vegetables colorful and pleasantly crisp.
rau-cu-xao-thap-cam-chay.finished_dish: The vegetables are colorful and just tender, the shiitake are aromatic, and a light coating of sauce clings without pooling on the plate.
rau-cu-xao-thap-cam-chay.serving: Serve hot as the vegetable dish in a vegetarian rice meal, alongside braised tofu and steamed rice.
tips: Cut vegetables to similar sizes for even cooking.
Blanch vegetables separately according to how quickly they cook; do not soften them fully.
Stir-fry quickly over high heat and add celery at the end to preserve its aroma.

rau-cu-xao-thap-cam-chay.media_alt_text: A plate of vegetarian mixed vegetables with broccoli, baby corn, carrots, peas, bell pepper, and shiitake.
rau-cu-xao-thap-cam-chay.time_note: About 60 minutes including preparation, blanching, and stir-frying; advance preparation can shorten active cooking.

preparation_steps: Separate the broccoli and cauliflower into small florets. Rinse the baby corn, peas, shiitake, and other vegetables. Slice the carrot, bell pepper, and onion; mince the leek.
Bring salted water to a boil. Blanch the carrot first, then blanch the broccoli, cauliflower, baby corn, peas, and shiitake in turn until just tender. Drain well.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sauté the leek until fragrant. Stir in the soy sauce, vegetarian oyster sauce, seasoning powder, and sugar.
Add the blanched vegetables, mushrooms, onion, and bell pepper. Toss quickly over high heat for 2–3 minutes until evenly coated.
Add the celery and pepper, taste, and turn off the heat while the vegetables retain a little crunch.

ga-hap-cai-be-xanh.name: Steamed Chicken with Mustard Greens
ga-hap-cai-be-xanh.serving_basis: One chicken weighing about 1.7 kg for four people.
ga-hap-cai-be-xanh.description: Chicken is gently simmered with onion, then finished in a steamer with mustard greens, carrot, and a fragrant garlic sauce. The greens stay lightly crisp and soak up the savory sauce.
ga-hap-cai-be-xanh.finished_dish: The chicken is tender and cooked through; the mustard greens remain bright with a slight bite, and a thin layer of garlic oyster-soy sauce coats each piece.
ga-hap-cai-be-xanh.serving: Arrange the chicken and greens on a large platter and spoon over some sauce. Serve the remaining sauce on the side.
tips: Start the chicken in cool water to help it cook evenly.
Blanch and drain the mustard greens before steaming them with the chicken.
Skim the simmering liquid and season the sauce gradually because oyster and soy sauces are already salty.

ga-hap-cai-be-xanh.media_alt_text: Sliced steamed chicken arranged over mustard greens with carrot and garlic sauce.
ga-hap-cai-be-xanh.time_note: About 70 minutes; simmering time varies with the chicken size and pot.
ingredients: Clean; use a dressed whole chicken.
Rinse well and separate stems and leaves.
Peel and slice, or cut into flower shapes.

preparation_steps: Rinse the chicken and drain it. Peel the onion and rinse the scallions; wash the mustard greens and carrot.
Separate the thick mustard stems from the leaves. Slice the carrot, mince the garlic, and prepare the sauce seasonings.
cooking_steps: Place the chicken in a pot of cool water with the onion and scallion whites. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for about 30–35 minutes, turning if needed for even doneness.
Blanch the mustard stems, leaves, and carrot until just tender. Arrange them on a heatproof platter, cut the chicken into serving pieces, place it on top, and steam for about 10 minutes.
Sauté the garlic in oil until fragrant. Add oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, pepper, and a little chicken broth; simmer for 2–3 minutes until lightly glossy.
Spoon some sauce over the chicken and steam for a further 5 minutes. Serve hot with the remaining sauce.

ga-cuon-bap-cai.name: Chicken Cabbage Rolls
aliases: Steamed Chicken Rolls in Cabbage Leaves
ga-cuon-bap-cai.serving_basis: About twelve small rolls for three people.
ga-cuon-bap-cai.description: Tender cabbage leaves wrap a chicken filling with water chestnut, ginger, and a little lime. Brief steaming keeps the rolls juicy and makes them a light centerpiece for a family meal.
ga-cuon-bap-cai.finished_dish: The cabbage leaves stay intact around the filling; the chicken is tender and fully cooked, with a slight crunch from water chestnut and a fresh citrus aroma.
ga-cuon-bap-cai.serving: Arrange the rolls on a platter and sprinkle with toasted sesame. Serve hot with chili soy sauce or a sweet-and-sour dip.
tips: Blanch cabbage leaves only until pliable so they are easy to roll without tearing.
Do not over-process the filling; retain some texture from the water chestnuts.
Make the rolls a consistent size and steam until the filling is completely cooked; larger rolls need more time.

ga-cuon-bap-cai.media_alt_text: Steamed cabbage rolls filled with chicken and water chestnuts, finished with sesame.
ga-cuon-bap-cai.time_note: About 30 minutes for small rolls; larger rolls need longer steaming.

preparation_steps: Separate intact cabbage leaves. Blanch them in lightly salted boiling water for 1–2 minutes until pliable, then transfer to cool water and drain.
Cut the chicken into small pieces. Peel and dice the water chestnuts; mince the garlic, ginger, scallions, and cilantro.
cooking_steps: Mince or pulse the chicken with garlic, ginger, scallions, cilantro, fish sauce, salt, lime juice, zest, and sesame oil until combined. Fold in the water chestnuts at the end.
Place a portion of filling near the base of a cabbage leaf. Fold in both sides and roll tightly. Set each roll seam-side down to hold its shape.
Arrange the rolls over steaming water and steam for about 8–10 minutes depending on size, until the chicken filling is fully cooked. Sprinkle with toasted sesame and serve hot.
